questions.question_text: Which of the following errors will not affect the agreement of a Trial Balance?
options: C) Error of posting to wrong side
D) Wrong balancing of an account
questions.answer: B) Error of principle

questions.question_text: The main objective of preparing a Trial Balance is to:
options: C) Check arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts
questions.answer: C) Check arithmetical accuracy of ledger accounts

questions.question_text: Depreciation is calculated on the:
options: C) Cost price of asset (under SLM)
questions.answer: C) Cost price of asset (under SLM)

questions.question_text: Under the Written Down Value method, the amount of depreciation goes on:
questions.answer: B) Decreasing every year

questions.question_text: A provision is created by debiting:
options: A) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
questions.answer: B) Profit and Loss Account

questions.question_text: Money spent on overhauling a second-hand machine purchased is considered as:
questions.answer: C) Capital Expenditure

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a Capital Receipt?
questions.answer: C) Sale of old machinery

questions.question_text: Wages paid for the installation of new machinery should be debited to:
questions.answer: B) Machinery Account

questions.question_text: According to the convention of conservatism, closing stock is valued at:
options: C) Cost price or Market price, whichever is lower
D) Cost price or Market price, whichever is higher
questions.answer: C) Cost price or Market price, whichever is lower

questions.question_text: Prepaid expenses appearing in the Trial Balance are shown in:
options: A) Profit and Loss Account only
B) Balance Sheet Assets side only
D) Both P&L and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: B) Balance Sheet Assets side only

questions.question_text: If outstanding wages appear outside the trial balance as an adjustment, they will be recorded in:
options: C) P&L A/c and Balance Sheet
D) Trading A/c and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: D) Trading A/c and Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: A Suspense Account is generally opened when:
options: A) Balance Sheet does not match
B) Trial Balance does not agree
C) Profit is to be calculated
questions.answer: B) Trial Balance does not agree

questions.question_text: Which of the following creates a Secret Reserve?
options: D) Creating provision for doubtful debts
questions.answer: A) Under-valuation of closing stock

questions.question_text: Goods withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use are credited to:
questions.answer: C) Purchases Account

questions.question_text: Bad debts recovered are treated as:
questions.answer: A) Revenue receipt

questions.question_text: Marshaling of Balance Sheet means:
options: B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order
questions.answer: B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order

questions.question_text: Loss of goods by fire is credited to:
questions.answer: B) Trading A/c

questions.question_text: Income received in advance is a:
questions.answer: B) Liability

questions.question_text: Which account is not closed by transferring its balance to Trading or P&L Account?
questions.answer: C) Machinery Account

questions.question_text: Amortization refers to writing off:
questions.answer: B) Intangible Assets

questions.question_text: Define a Suspense Account and state its primary purpose in accounting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Suspense Account is a temporary account used to record the difference in a Trial Balance when it does not tally, helping to delay rectification until errors are found.

questions.question_text: State two main causes of depreciation on fixed assets. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The two main causes of depreciation are physical wear and tear from continuous use, and obsolescence due to technological advancements or changes in market demand.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between Capital Expenditure and Revenue Expenditure based on their earning capacity. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Capital expenditure increases the earning capacity or efficiency of the business, whereas revenue expenditure is incurred to maintain the existing earning capacity of the assets.

questions.question_text: Explain the treatment of 'Outstanding Wages' provided outside the Trial Balance as an adjustment. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Outstanding wages given in adjustments are added to wages on the debit side of the Trading Account and shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: What is the convention of grouping and marshaling in a Balance Sheet? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Grouping means putting items of similar nature under a common heading, while marshaling refers to arranging assets and liabilities in the order of liquidity or permanence.

questions.question_text: State the accounting treatment when goods are distributed as free samples. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The cost of free samples is debited to Advertisement Account (Profit & Loss A/c) and credited to the Purchases Account (Trading A/c) as it reduces stock.

questions.question_text: Rectify the following error: Sales Book was undercast by $500. Provide the journal entry assuming a suspense account was opened. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: An undercast in the Sales Book means the Sales Account is short by $500. The rectifying entry is to Debit Suspense A/c $500 and Credit Sales A/c $500, thereby increasing the sales balance to its correct amount.

questions.question_text: A machine was bought for $50,000, installation costs were $5,000, and estimated scrap value is $5,000 after 10 years. Calculate the annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Total cost of the machine is $55,000 ($50k + $5k). Depreciable amount is $50,000 ($55,000 cost - $5,000 scrap). Annual depreciation is $50,000 / 10 years = $5,000 per year under the Straight Line Method.

questions.question_text: Provide the adjusting journal entry for accrued commission of $1,200 at the end of the year, and state its impact on financial statements. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The journal entry is: Debit Accrued Commission A/c $1,200; Credit Commission A/c $1,200. This increases the total commission income on the credit side of P&L and creates a current asset on the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Explain how a 'Secret Reserve' is created in a business without explicitly showing it in the books. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A secret reserve is created by intentionally understating assets or overstating liabilities. Common methods include writing off excessive depreciation, undervaluing closing stock, or charging capital expenditures directly to the Profit and Loss account.

questions.question_text: Rectify the error: Machinery purchased for $10,000 was wrongly debited to the Purchases Account. Provide the rectifying entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: This is an error of principle. The rectifying journal entry is: Debit Machinery Account $10,000 to record the asset, and Credit Purchases Account $10,000 to reverse the incorrect expense charge.

questions.question_text: Calculate Gross Profit if Cost of Goods Sold is $120,000 and Sales are made at a profit of 20% on Sales. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: If profit is 20% on sales, cost represents 80% of sales. Let Sales be S. 0.80S = $120,000, so Sales = $150,000. Gross Profit equals Sales minus COGS, which is $150,000 - $120,000 = $30,000.

questions.question_text: How do you treat 'Goods costing $4,000 destroyed by fire, insurance company admitted a claim for $3,000' in final accounts? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Deduct $4,000 from Purchases in the Trading Account. Show the insurance claim of $3,000 on the Assets side of the Balance Sheet. Debit the net unrecovered loss of $1,000 to the Profit & Loss Account.

questions.question_text: Distinguish between a Provision and a Reserve regarding their nature and necessity. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A provision is a charge against profit created for a known liability of uncertain amount, mandatory even if there are losses. A reserve is an appropriation of profit for future contingencies, created only when adequate profits exist.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: From the trial balance, Sundry Debtors are $60,000 and Bad Debts are $1,500. Adjustments: Write off further bad debts of $3,000 and maintain a Provision for Doubtful Debts at 5%. Detail the P&L and Balance Sheet presentation. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, deduct further bad debts ($3,000) from Debtors, leaving $57,000. Calculate new provision: 5% of $57,000 = $2,850. In P&L debit, sum Bad Debts ($1,500) + Further Bad Debts ($3,000) + New Provision ($2,850) = $7,350 total expense. In Balance Sheet Assets, show Debtors at $57,000 less $2,850 provision, netting $54,150.

questions.question_text: A company bought a machine for $100,000 on April 1, 2023. Depreciation is 10% p.a. on Written Down Value. Describe the balances in the Machinery Account at the end of Year 1, Year 2, and Year 3 (March 31, 2026). [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Year 1 depreciation is $10,000; closing WDV is $90,000. Year 2 depreciation is 10% of $90,000 = $9,000; closing WDV is $81,000. Year 3 depreciation is 10% of $81,000 = $8,100; closing WDV on March 31, 2026, is $72,900. The asset will reflect at $72,900 in the final Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: A Trial Balance disagreed and the difference was placed in Suspense. Find the rectifying entries for: (i) $1,000 paid for repairs debited to Building A/c. (ii) $500 discount received not posted to Discount A/c. Explain the Suspense impact. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: (i) Error of principle: Debit Repairs $1,000, Credit Building $1,000 (No Suspense impact). (ii) Omission in ledger: Debit Suspense $500, Credit Discount Received $500. This entry adds $500 to the credit side of the Trial Balance, clearing the corresponding $500 debit difference previously resting in the Suspense Account.

questions.question_text: Construct the layout of a Trading Account for the year ended March 31, 2026, detailing Opening Stock $20,000, Purchases $80,000, Purchase Returns $2,000, Wages $10,000, Sales $150,000, and Closing Stock $25,000. Determine the Gross Profit. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: On the debit side: Opening Stock $20,000 + Net Purchases ($80,000 - $2,000 = $78,000) + Wages $10,000 = Total debits of $108,000. On the credit side: Sales $150,000 + Closing Stock $25,000 = Total credits of $175,000. The difference is the Gross Profit: $175,000 - $108,000 = $67,000, transferred to P&L.
